subject: Latency credit banding proposal + order-form runbook
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@medisight.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@medisight.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Custom latency bands & order-form / runbook request

Marissa —

Thanks for the uptime conversation last week. As we scope the pilot for our imaging-assist inference endpoints, procurement needs a clear, order-form-ready SLA that includes latency credit tiers rather than a single flat uptime credit structure. For our clinicians the difference between ~120ms and ~450ms P95 is material.

Attached is a short note from our SRE showing the latency sensitivity and a suggested credit model we drafted (medisight-sla-request-aug22.pdf). Can Redwood draft: (1) order-form language that maps credit percentages to latency bands (P95/P99), and (2) an ops-runbook outline that describes Redwood's automatic mitigations, expected evidence (telemetry), and incident notification timelines? We also need any DocuSign-ready exhibit language so procurement can attach it to the MSA quickly.

Timeline: we'd like a first pass by EOD Tuesday (PST) to keep legal on track.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short sync if helpful.

—Elena
Director, Platform Operations
MediSight Health
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@medisight.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Custom latency bands & order-form / runbook request

Elena — thanks for the note and the attachment. We're aligned on the ask. Below is a proposed structure we can convert into order-form exhibit language and an ops-runbook appendix:

1) Latency credit banding (applies to P95 latency measured per billing period per route):
   - Band A (P95 <= 150ms): 0% credit (target/nominal)
   - Band B (150ms < P95 <= 300ms): 10% monthly service credit
   - Band C (300ms < P95 <= 700ms): 25% monthly service credit
   - Band D (P95 > 700ms): 50% monthly service credit and escalation to dedicated capacity review

2) P99 threshold clause (for severe tail events): if P99 exceeds 2x configured model baseline for >72 cumulative minutes in a 30-day window, customer is eligible for an additional remediation credit and on-call RCA.

3) Mitigation & fallback (ops-runbook summary):
   - Automatic model fallback to a compatible lower-latency quantized variant when sustained P95 degradation exceeds Band C for 15 minutes.
   - Regional routing to secondary region within 5 minutes for routing-capable customers.
   - Prefix/KV cache flushback guidance and recommended client-timeouts.

4) Evidence & reporting:
   - Monthly latency report (per-route P50/P90/P95/P99) + daily alert summary on incidents.
   - Raw telemetry export (anonymized request-level latency, route id, model id) available on request under NDA.

5) Notification & timing:
   - Automated alert at threshold breach (15m sustained in Band C).
   - 24-hour acknowledgement and initial incident summary; full RCA within 7 business days for Band D / P99 events.

I've attached a quick draft PDF (redwood-latency-band-draft.pdf) and a skeleton runbook (ops-runbook-outline.md). Kim — can you please review the order-form exhibit wording and confirm whether the Band percentages and the fallback language are acceptable from a legal/contracting perspective? Karthik / Priyom — please advise on the operational feasibility for the automatic fallback and telemetry exports; if there are constraints we should call them out in the exhibit as configuration flags.

Elena — I can turn this into DocuSign-ready exhibit language once legal signs off; I think we can hit your Tuesday EOD ask if everyone moves quickly. If useful I'll schedule a 30-min sync with procurement/legal today.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@medisight.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-23T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Custom latency bands & order-form / runbook request

Marissa / Elena —

Thanks for the clear proposal. High-level comments and suggested order-form language below. I kept the structure banded to make it easy for procurement to review and attach as an exhibit to the MSA/SOW.

Suggested redline summary (order-form exhibit):
- Insert new "Latency Credit Exhibit" referencing route identifiers and measurement window.
- Define measurement method: P95 computed on request-level latency measured at Redwood ingress, excluding client-side timeouts and maintenance windows announced >= 72 hours in advance.
- Credit table (copy bands from Marissa) + clear cap: Credits are applied to Redwood invoice for the impacted billing period and may not exceed 100% of the monthly subscription charge for the impacted route.
- Evidence delivery: Monthly aggregated report + exportable telemetry within 3 business days of a written request.
- Dispute window: Customer must raise billing credit disputes within 45 days of invoice issuance.
- Exceptions: Force majeure and scheduled maintenance (with notice) excluded; any dedicated capacity exceptions to be separately scheduled.

Operational notes / legal asks:
- We should avoid prescriptive mitigation language that creates an operational SLA ("must perform fallback within X minutes") unless the customer purchases Dedicated capacity. Let's keep fallback described as "automatic fallback may be employed where available and configured by the customer; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to route to compatible variants and regions." This prevents strict uptime obligations while preserving our intent.
- Require a standardized telemetry request process (HubSpot ticket + signed NDA) for raw exports to limit data leakage.

If that language looks good to Elena, Marissa, I'll prepare a DocuSign-ready exhibit and confirm the DocuSign routing (legal approval required).

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@medisight.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@medisight.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Custom latency bands & order-form / runbook request

Thanks, all — this is exactly the level of detail procurement/legal needed. A few quick follow-ups: 

- Medisight prefers the more prescriptive mitigation timing if possible (we'd like to call out the 15-minute auto-fallback behavior). If Redwood needs that gated to Dedicated, please state that clearly so we can weigh the procurement delta.
- Telemetry NDA: understood. We'll run your suggested HubSpot+NDA flow; can you add the exact HubSpot form/link in the exhibit?
- DocuSign & timeline: We accept the Band table and evidence cadence. Please generate the DocuSign-ready exhibit and send to my procurement inbox. If you can get the DocuSign link by tomorrow EOD PST we'll start internal signoff the same day.

Also note: our infra team flagged a potential need for on-prem/air-gapped option later in the contract term. Can Redwood include a placeholder sentence in the exhibit indicating an option for private deployment pricing and SLA details to be added as an addendum? That will keep our procurement roadmap cleaner.

Happy to do a quick 15-min sync if Kimberly or Marissa want to walk through the DocuSign exhibit before sending.

—Elena
